studies.label: Three-arm laboratory experiment: alternative solutions and campaign briefs

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 182), Sections 3.1-3.2, randomized conditions and participants; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1, analyzed total and arm counts
counts_source.quote: A total of 480 undergraduate students participated across three broad disciplinary clusters. ... Condition 1: Unaided Control (𝑛= 160): ... Condition 2: Unconstrained GenAI Access (𝑛= 160): ... Condition 3: Structured Scaffolding (𝑛= 160):

arms.name: Unaided Control
arms.description: Unaided creative problem solving and ideation; no digital devices, search engines, or AI interfaces permitted (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Unconstrained GenAI Access
arms.description: Unmonitored LLM interface access, with permission to use it in any manner to complete the tasks (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Structured Scaffolding
arms.description: The same LLM interface under the Cognitive Anchor-Rebound Protocol: generate at least three own ideas before opening it, interrogate ideas using critique and counter-factual prompts, and synthesize without copying AI text (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

studies.task: In one 90-minute session, students proposed sustainable solutions to microplastic contamination in the Mekong Delta and wrote a 600-word campaign brief for a socio-technological enterprise addressing rural education equity (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.3).

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 182), Section 3.1, Unconstrained GenAI Access and Structured Scaffolding; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 189), Section 8, Model Evolution: models described as available in 2024–2026; individual release years and model allocation are not stated

preregistration.where: No preregistration statement in the complete saved paper.

sources.quote: However, their expert-rated Originality scores plummeted (𝑀= 3.41 vs. 𝑀= 4.82, 𝑝< .001, 𝑑= −1.34).

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports composite scores and participant counts. SDs are coded at the participant level, rather than treating the separate expert ratings as independent observations. The pairwise total is not separately printed and is not calculated; n_total is null. The three-arm omnibus ANOVA is not entered as this pairwise test. Its printed row, under F(2, 477), p-value, and η², is: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1, "Originality (CAT 1- 7) 4.82 (1.15) 3.41 (0.94) 5.44 (0.88) 165.23 <.001 .409". The paper names this among its primary dependent variables in Section 4.1; preregistration is not stated. The standardizer for the printed d and its uncertainty are not stated; the post-hoc test statistic is not printed. The main-results d conflicts with the abstract. The abstract states: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 179), Abstract, "it produced a statistically significant reduction in conceptual originality (𝑑= −0.58, 𝑝< .001) compared to the unaided control group.". The discrepancy is unresolved; the main-results value is transcribed without recomputation. The Discussion box also prints "Conceptual Originality: -29.2% Drop (d = -1.34)" (PDF p. 9 (printed p. 187), Section 6, discussion box); its percentage calculation is not explained.

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports composite scores and participant counts. SDs are coded at the participant level, rather than treating the separate expert ratings as independent observations. estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large embeddings; pairwise cosine similarity of student submissions within the same task and condition. The paper describes a 1536-dimensional vector space. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.4, item 3; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 185), Section 4.2 and Table 2.

sources.quote: The mean pairwise cosine similarity between student submissions in the Unconstrained GenAI condition was 𝜌= 0.689, compared to 𝜌= 0.412in the Unaided Control group (𝑡(318) = 34.21, 𝑝< .001, 𝑑= 3.79).

estimates.notes: Computed over pairs of different students' submissions within each condition and task. Table 2 does not identify the task or explain the aggregation into analysis observations; unit and n_units are therefore null. Table 2 does not print analysis-specific participant counts. The study arm counts appear in Table 1, but counts for this diversity calculation are unconfirmed; n_treatment, n_control, and n_total are null and are not inferred from degrees of freedom. The paper names Semantic Distance among its primary dependent variables, but preregistration is not stated. The printed arm SDs are retained, but what they are taken over is not specified; sd_level and the inferential unit remain unknown. Higher values mean outputs are more similar. The paper does not identify the t-test subtype, observations supplied to the test, or the standardizer for d. Its t-test and positive d are recorded in similarity units/sign convention; the direction is not reversed during extraction.

open_items: Originality has conflicting printed standardized effects for Unconstrained GenAI Access versus Unaided Control. PDF p. 1 (printed p. 179), Abstract: "it produced a statistically significant reduction in conceptual originality (𝑑= −0.58, 𝑝< .001) compared to the unaided control group."; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Section 4.1: "However, their expert-rated Originality scores plummeted (𝑀= 3.41 vs. 𝑀= 4.82, 𝑝< .001, 𝑑= −1.34).". The correct intended effect is not established by the PDF.

Fluency has conflicting omnibus statistics: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 179), Abstract: "while unconstrained GenAI access significantly increased task fluency (𝐹(2,477) = 48.21, 𝑝< .001, 𝜂2 = .168)"; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1, under F(2, 477), p-value, and η²: "Fluency (Count) 5.12 (1.42) 11.45 (2.85) 8.84 (1.95) 284.15 <.001 .543".

The diversity analysis does not establish analysis-specific participant counts, the number of observations, SD level, aggregation, or t-test subtype. No participant-level uncertainty is assumed from the reported degrees of freedom (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4; PDF p. 7, printed p. 185, Section 4.2).

The tasks underlying the TTCT outcomes and Table 2 diversity measures, and any combination across tasks, are not specified. CAT ratings explicitly concern project briefs (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4).

The allocation procedure and participant flow/exclusions are not described. Matching condition and analyzed counts are transcribed, without asserting that no exclusions occurred (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 184, Table 1).

Which students used each named LLM, how model choice was made, and the individual model release years are not supplied. Section 8 reports only an availability period; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 189, Section 8).

The standardizers and uncertainty for the printed d values are not stated. Most pairwise test statistics, pairwise SEs, and confidence intervals are absent (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184, Section 4.1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 185, Section 4.2).
The TTCT raters' qualifications are not stated, leaving the Elaboration measure category unclassified (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4).
The percentage changes in the discussion box have no stated calculation; they are retained as printed and not recomputed (PDF p. 9, printed p. 187, Section 6).
The named MANOVA dependent-variable list differs from the outcomes in Table 1; the precise multivariate specification is not established (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184, Section 4.1).
notes: The entire markdown was read through its final reference entry, and PDF text was extracted for every cited page. Tables 1 and 2 were recovered with PyMuPDF find_tables and used for direct transcription. The saved paper contains no appended supplement; the Appendix of Algorithmic Contribution in Table 4 is a proposed student deliverable (PDF p. 11, printed p. 189). Only the named extraction file is written. No statistics, totals, percentages, or standardized effects are calculated. Table 1 contains six output measures, each recorded for all three arm comparisons. The two Table 2 diversity columns are recorded separately for completeness and explicitly identified as equivalent transformations of the same submissions. The three-arm omnibus tests are not pairwise treatment effects. The ASCII originality-versus-fluency graphic supplies no exact labeled observations; no coordinates are read from it, and the tabulated values are used (PDF p. 7, printed p. 185). Initial unaided ideation in the scaffolded protocol precedes AI use; the paper reports no separately scored task after AI removal. No preregistration or cross-paper sample-overlap statement is reported. The bibliography ends at Bose# in the saved PDF (PDF p. 12, printed p. 190); no continuation is present.
